sections.title: An Informational Poem
sections.content:
Stanley R. Greenfield's RFC is titled Remembrances of Things Past. It is presented as a poem under the heading Discussion, and its status section says it provides information rather than specifying an Internet standard.

The poem looks back at computing and networking vocabulary through rhyming comparisons. It is signed with the initials --srg.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC is a poem, not a protocol. It uses rhyme to look back at technical words and their other meanings.

sections.title: Technical Words and Everyday Meanings
sections.content:
The poem contrasts technical terms with ordinary uses. It says a router was a tool, a server was a maid, windows were for looking out of, bridges were for crossing, and a buffer was for buffing.

It also plays on names from computing, business, and popular culture. The joke depends on words acquiring new meanings as they become part of technical vocabulary.
sections.plainLanguage: The poem takes familiar computer terms and reminds the reader that the same words once meant other things. The contrast is the source of its humor.

sections.title: The Closing Toast
sections.content:
The final lines look ahead to growth in memory and operating speed. They toast the possibility of further increases in the following year.

The RFC's Security Considerations section says that security issues are not discussed in the memo.
sections.plainLanguage: The poem ends by wishing for more memory and faster computers. It includes no technical recommendations.
